items.prose: Two bars of an electronic music box playing an 18th-century folk tune, followed by a synthesized female voice reciting five-figure groups: '0-4-2-9-1... 8-8-3-1-0...' The transmission runs without variation every four hours from a coastal transmitter site powered by a decaying RTG.

A metallic, high-pitched mechanical music box chime that speeds up slightly as the clockwork spring winds down, followed by a child's voice: 'Achtung! 5-5-2... 1-0-9...' In the radio room, dwellers listen in absolute silence, wondering if the child was recorded forty years ago or yesterday.

The magnetic audio tape loop has degraded from twenty years of exposure to damp bunker air. The introductory flute melody wobbles with extreme wow and flutter, followed by a hiss of oxide flaking off the plastic backing. An open microphone in the transmitter vault picks up the distant sound of dripping groundwater.

A monotonous 25-tone per minute buzzer pulse on 4625 kHz. For sixteen years, it has held the frequency open like an automated heartbeat. At 04:12 on Day 3,412, the buzzer suddenly dropped carrier and a raspy human voice read: 'ANNA-BORIS-7-4-1-9-0-ZAPAL' before the buzzer slammed back on.

A strange warbling acoustic modulation that sweeps from 800 Hz down to 200 Hz, sounding like a descending copper whistle. Analysis on a spectrum analyzer reveals multi-layered phonetic audio tracks played backwards at quadruple speed—an automated high-speed burst transmitter awaiting acknowledgment from ghost submarines.

Four pure sinusoidal tones (440, 554, 659, 880 Hz) struck in ascending sequence, followed by two minutes of dead unmodulated carrier. A bunker engineer noted that the four tones match the acoustic resonant frequencies of the main intake damper solenoids in Government Bunker 04.

A harsh, barking male voice repeating standard phonetic alphabet pairs against background 60-cycle generator rumble: 'BRAVO-TANGO... ECHO-KILO... SIERRA-WHISKEY...' The recording cuts off mid-word every fourteen minutes when the mechanical drum player resets its head.

Hand-keyed Morse code sent at eight words per minute on the old 500 kHz maritime distress band. The message loops endlessly from an automated mechanical code wheel: 'ALL STATIONS CLOSE LOGS STOP PRIME POWER FAILING STOP GOD PRESERVE US STOP VAULT 07 OUT STOP SK'.
